items.text: After the head of internal audit flagged the inventory gaps, the CEO told her he did not want to know and stopped attending the monthly reviews.
The compliance officer warned the CFO about channel partners. The CFO instructed his staff not to forward any more of her emails.
There is no allegation that the CEO declined to review any report or was told of any problem.
The chief executive made a point of staying uninformed about the irregularities his staff kept raising and arranged to be left off the distribution.
Customers complained repeatedly about failed units and the warnings reached the COO, who took no action.
Plaintiffs fail to allege that any defendant received a warning about the reserve.
Weekly pipeline reports sent to the CEO showed bookings down 30 percent while he reaffirmed guidance on the earnings call.
Even after receiving the engineers' memo, the CEO continued to assure investors that the recall was isolated.
On May 2, 2022 the CFO sold 64% of his shares. On June 10, 2022 the company announced the restatement and the stock fell 38%.
The CEO sold stock three weeks before the corrective disclosure, far more than in any prior year.
The CFO sold shares pursuant to a pre-existing 10b5-1 plan adopted before the class period, consistent with his prior trading.
The CEO adopted a 10b5-1 plan two weeks before the guidance cut and began selling under it.
The CFO abruptly resigned ten days before the company disclosed the accounting review.
The outside auditor resigned and withdrew its opinion on the 2021 financial statements.
The controller deleted the emails about the side agreements after the subpoena arrived.
Sales managers used side letters granting return rights and kept them from the auditors.
The CEO's bonus was tied to meeting the revenue target he announced to the market.
Defendants were motivated to maintain a high stock price.
In the last week of each quarter the team shipped product early with extended payment terms to hit guidance.
The CFO signed SOX certifications in March 2021 weeks after the controller warned him about the reserve releases.
The company designs industrial sensors and sells them through distributors in Europe and Asia.
The district court dismissed the complaint with leave to amend.
